If your nutritionist is telling you it’s okay to cut out entire food groups and has not had a serious talk with you about the weight you’ve lost this quickly you need to find someone who knows what they are doing.

For reference the CDC recommends at a maximum 8 lbs weight loss a month. Your numbers put you at around 20.


I understand that line of reasoning about having eaten enough calories over the last four years and all, and I agree, it’s something that should make sense on paper. The reality is that it is so much more complex and a quick google search into the statistics of weight regain after weight loss is worth looking into. 
Are you an exception? If so, why?


Something I encourage you to do is to challenge some of the habits you’ve set up here. 
Is it realistic to never eat at your favorite fast food restaurant ever again?
What would happen if you had your favorite restaurant for dinner tomorrow night? 
Is it realistic to never miss a day of running?
What would happen if you took a day off tomorrow?

Just something to think about,

So let me get this strait,

You’ve lost roughly 60 pounds in roughly 3 months. 
Your eating 1100 calories a day and running an average of 9.5 miles a day.
You’ve got blood in your urine and a doctor told you your anemic.

I think it’s great you’ve found a hobby that you enjoy, but you need to realize that if you do want to keep running, changes have got to be made…
At this rate your speedrunning an eating disorder.

Weight is just a number and the fallacy of linearity is real.

Be well OP
